Definition: Affordability of mobile broadband data, measured as the cost of a basic mobile data plan (1-2GB) as a percentage of GNI per capita. The UN Broadband Commission target is below 2% of monthly GNI per capita. Affordability is the single largest barrier to internet adoption in Africa.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: No source cited for the original 'Expensive (5-10%)' claim. Cable.co.uk/Voronoi (2023) put Gabon's average 1GB mobile data price at ~US$4.09, and the mAccess Diagnostic Tool records US$5.07 for a 1GB prepaid basket; against World Bank GNI per capita of US$7,790 (2024, Atlas method, ~US$649/month) this implies roughly 0.6-1.2% of monthly GNI per capita for a 1-2GB basket, well below the 'Expensive' band. Revised down to Affordable (1-2%); flagged for human review as no single ITU-published country % of GNI figure for the standard 2GB basket could be located to confirm precisely.

Definition: The country's total international internet bandwidth capacity per internet user, indicating the quality and capacity of the country's connection to the global internet. Determined by submarine cable landings (for coastal states), cross-border terrestrial fibre (for landlocked states), and satellite links.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: No source cited originally. ITU/TheGlobalEconomy data show international bandwidth per internet user of 19.66 kbit/s in 2016 (2013-2016 average 12.39 kbit/s); a World Bank Central African Backbone Program report cites 11.84 kbit/s per internet user in 2017. Both fall in the 5-19 kbit/s 'Low' band, so the code is confirmed, but the most recent verifiable figure is 8-9 years old — flagged for human review to locate a post-2020 ITU DataHub figure.

redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: No source cited for the original 80%+ claim, and no Gabon-specific smartphone-adoption percentage could be verified. Revised to Unknown (0) pending a country-specific GSMA Intelligence figure; recommend human review.

Definition: Affordability of electricity for residential and small business consumers, measured as cost of electricity relative to income levels. High electricity costs are a direct barrier to ICT adoption and data center viability.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: No source cited originally. GlobalPetrolPrices (December 2025) records a residential tariff of US$0.214/kWh, consistent with SEEG's own published tariff schedule. Against World Bank GNI per capita of US$7,790 (2024, ~US$649/month), a benchmark 100kWh/month basic-consumption cost of ~US$21.40 is ~3.3% of monthly GNI per capita, consistent with 'Moderate (3-5%)'. Confirmed, though the precise percentage is sensitive to the assumed consumption level (1.6-4.9% across a 50-150kWh range).

Definition: The proportion of the population with basic digital skills (ability to use a computer, smartphone, or the internet for simple tasks such as sending messages, finding information, or using apps). Based on ITU household survey data, Afrobarometer, or national ICT surveys.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: No source cited originally, and no ITU/UNESCO figure for the share of Gabon's population with basic digital skills could be located. The only partial proxy found is Afrobarometer's Digital Economy Readiness index (Round 9, 2021-23), which places Gabon among four countries (with Mauritius, Seychelles, Morocco) where more than three-quarters of citizens have 'moderate or full' readiness — but this composite measures device/electricity/internet access, not self-reported digital skills, so it cannot directly confirm or refute the 60%+ claim. Left unchanged; flagged for human review pending a direct ITU household ICT-skills figure for Gabon.
